title: Draining a peritonsillar abscess
what: The doctor opens the abscess next to the tonsil and lets the pus out. This quickly relieves pain and pressure.
why: When, after tonsillitis, one side of your throat hurts badly, and it is hard to open your mouth and swallow.
duration: the procedure usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; sometimes you need to stay in the hospital for a few days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners
Allergies to antibiotics and numbing medicine
If it is hard to breathe, say so right away

prepare.title: Urgent
prepare.text: This is urgent care. Do not put off the visit.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually you do not eat before the procedure, but if it is urgent, tell the doctor when you last ate.

prepare.title: Your things
prepare.text: Bring things in case you need to stay in the hospital.

bring: Things for 1 to 3 days in the hospital
steps: Sometimes a test needle or an ultrasound is used
Your throat is numbed with a spray and an injection
A small cut is made and the pus is let out
Antibiotics are prescribed, often through a vein
feel: During the procedure, you feel pressure, and it may hurt
After the abscess is opened, you usually feel better quickly
after: Drink fluids and eat soft, warm food
Gargle and take medicines as prescribed
Sometimes the area is opened again the next day
Later, the doctor may talk with you about removing the tonsils
red_flags: It is hard to breathe, or your neck is very swollen: call emergency services
Blood from the mouth: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C that does not go down

faq.q: Will the abscess go away on its own?
faq.a: Usually not. The pus needs to be let out, or the infection can spread.

faq.q: Do my tonsils need to be removed?
faq.a: Sometimes, yes, if the abscess comes back. The doctor decides.

reminders.text: Do not put off your visit. If it is hard to breathe, call emergency services.
